steps: Boil the eggs in water on medium for about 10 minutes, cool them in cold water, then peel and prick them with a fork.
Heat the oil on medium, add the cumin and bay leaf, and wait until they sizzle.
Add the onion and fry, stirring, for about 8 minutes, until golden brown.
Stir in the ginger, garlic and green chilli for 1 to 2 minutes, until the raw smell goes.
Add the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala and salt; cover and cook 5 to 7 minutes until soft.
Turn the heat to low, stir in the whisked curd and cook until oil shows at the edges.
Add the eggs and about 80 ml water a person, cover and simmer on medium-low for about 8 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Turn off the heat and finish with the crushed kasuri methi and coriander leaves.
note: Two eggs a person, with the gravy scaled to match. The three sources used between 1 and 1.7 eggs a person, so the onion and tomato follow the two richer recipes.
